newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crudes firmer, Dubai intermonth bids rise.
newsitem.headline: Asian crudes firmer, Dubai intermonth bids rise.

text.p: Asian crude prices were higher on Monday with Middle East prices staying firm and Dubai intermonth bids rising.
Wet Dubai cargoes for January were traded at full month quotes plus 72 cents and plus 77 cents, reflecting a firmer tone elsewhere on MidEast grades.
Traders said Murban cargos changed hands Friday between 60 and 62 cents per barrel, off from a 65-cent deal done earlier last week, but holding the generally firm levels seen in recent weeks.
Futures markets showed stronger prices with January Brent rising seven cents per barrel to $23.10 in late SIMEX trading from the London settlement of $23.03.
NYMEX January crude on ACCESS was last traded at $23.76 per barrel, up one cent from New York but off the intraday traded high of $23.80.
The latest Dubai wet deals surpassed previous traded levels by five to 10 cents per barrel.

Brokers said the news pushed the bid on January/February and February/March up to 50 cents by late Monday, up from talked levels earlier in the day of 46 cents and 45 cents respectively. Brokers said there were no indicated offers, although notionally they put offers around 57 cents for January/February and 55 for February/March.

Oman crude was holding premiums of 13 cents per barrel, traders said. They said a Japanese trader had bought two cargos at plus 13 cents and another at plus 12 cents on Friday and Monday. The deals were not confirmed
